g.text: 1. user should be able to select pickup location and
drop location and get estimated price
2. user should be able to request a ride based on the estimate fare
3. upon request, rider should be matched with different riders who is nearby and availability
4. rider be able to accept/decline request
1.system should be highly consistent on ride matching single match for a ride
and for all other case highly avaiable system
3. system should be able to handle high throughput , specially during peak time
and events (100k request from same location)
2.DRIVER - who register as a transportive serivce
4.RIDE - represent full cycle of a ride -> from request to ending
5.LOCATION - store the real time location of driver
1. // select location and get estimate price
3. // matched with different riders. -> this will happen at the backendso no end point required
Note1: handle frequent driver location updates and efficient proximity searches on location data
solution1 : use batched based process with gradtree(POSTGSI) (on postgres db)
driver location update directly to the database, updates are aggregated over a short interval
batched process is used for reducing the number of write operations to a database
for proximity search will use geospatial database - guadtree index driver location
quadtree: well-suited for two-dimensional spatial data like geographic coordinates, as they partition the space
into quadrants recursively, which can significantly speed up the process of finding all drivers within a certain area
solution2 : use redis in-memory with geospatial datasotre(geohasing)
-redis support geospatial datatype, use geohasing for encoding lat & long coordinates
-allows us to handle real-time driver location updates and proximity searches with high throughput
and low latency while minimizing storage costs with automatic data expiration.
challenges: Redis is an in-memory data store, there's a risk of data loss in case of a system crash or power failure
-use redis persistence: enable redis presistence mechanism like RDB (REDIS DATABSE) or AOF (Append-on-file)
-Redis Sentinel: We could use Redis Sentinel for high availability.
Sentinel provides automatic failover if the master node goes down, ensuring that a replica is promoted to master.
ondevice sensors and algorithms to determine the optimal interval
check if a user have a outstanidng ride request
note 2: prevent multiple ride requests from being sent to the same driver simultaneously
both solution are good but will go with redis.
solution 1 : database status update with timout handling (status : outstanding_request on driver )
issue : to many write on database for this update when sending notification to driver on accept/deny
& Ride Service crashes or is restarted, the timeout will be lost and the lock will remain indefinitely.
solution2: distributed lock implemented in-memory like redis
(no ride request drop during peak demand)
sharding our data geographically and using read replicas to improve read throughput.
services, message queue, databases -- all of which can be sharded geographically
but , we would need to scatter gather (i.e., query multiple shards) when proximity search on a boundary
